reveal_asymmetry_note: Bimodal, not a single population. Five doors are square-on and show BOTH returns at near-equal width (ratios 0.95, 0.96, 1.00, 1.15, 1.29); four are shot off-axis and show one deep return against a hairline on the other side (5.5, 6.7, 9.2, 9.5). A renderer should switch between these two states rather than interpolate the median.

detail.note: Seven of ten carry line work. Only two of those are true milled grooves (d038, d034 - the lines read 0.3-0.8x the face). Four are APPLIED strips - polished stainless, brushed steel or pale brass - that read 1.1x to 2x BRIGHTER than the face. d063's four horizontal lines are shadow grooves. Getting the sign of that contrast wrong is the single easiest way to render this tier incorrectly.

vocabulary: ring knocker on a diamond backplate
ornate bow pull across the middle rail
brass strip inlaid into a black pull bar
mezuzah case (stainless hammered, and dark with gilt lettering)
characteristic: A designed door is a plain slab that has had one graphic idea applied to it: line work. Seven of the ten carry ruled lines - and in four of those the lines are applied metal strips that read BRIGHTER than the paint (up to 2x), not milled shadow grooves, which is the opposite of what the cheaper tier does; two more use classical raised panels instead. The hardware follows the same logic: six of ten drop the lever entirely for a long vertical pull bar (median 0.55 of the leaf height, up to 0.86), leaving only a round cylinder rose at the stile, and two doors carry a second decorative pull as well. The frame stays out of the way - nine of ten are painted the same colour as the leaf (face luminance 0.93x the leaf), so the whole opening reads as one mass and the only thing separating leaf from frame is the reveal shadow, median 0.044 of leaf width at tone 0.45, darkening from 0.68 at the head to 0.32 at the floor.
